title: Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients into the United States
key_claim: A Section 232 national-security tariff on patented pharmaceuticals and APIs is imposed on the finding that offshore production threatens US supply security, with tiered rates and onshoring/MFN relief.
frame_summary: The US is using national-security tariff powers as industrial policy to force pharmaceutical manufacturing back onshore.
signals_supported: US pharma tariffs and MFN pricing
verbatim_quote: According to the Food and Drug Administration, as of 2025, approximately 53 percent of patented pharmaceutical products distributed domestically are produced outside the country.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: Section 232 Tariffs on Pharmaceuticals: 100% Duties on Patented Drugs and APIs Starting July 31, 2026
date_evidence: April 14, 2026  Section 232 Tariffs on Pharmaceuticals: 100% Duties on Patented Drugs and APIs Starting July 31, 2026
key_claim: A 100% Section 232 duty on patented pharmaceuticals and APIs takes effect 31 July 2026 for Annex III firms and 29 September 2026 for others; EU/Japan/Korea/Switzerland rate 15%, UK 10%, onshoring firms 20%; 13 Annex II firms with MFN agreements exempt until 20 January 2029.
frame_summary: The Section 232 pharma tariff is a phased, tiered duty engineered to reward US onshoring and most-favoured-nation pricing deals.
signals_supported: US pharma tariffs and MFN pricing
verbatim_quote: an additional 100% duty will apply to certain patented pharmaceuticals and associated ingredients, including active pharmaceutical ingredients and key starting materials beginning on July 31, 2026.
verbatim_list: For subject patented pharmaceuticals and APIs that are products of the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein, the Section 232 duty rate will be 15%.
For subject patented pharmaceuticals and APIs that are products of the United Kingdom, the Section 232 duty rate will be 10%.

Products of 13 companies (listed in Annex II) that entered into most favored nation pricing agreements with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (“HHS”) will not be subject to any additional Section 232 tariff, until January 20, 2029.

title: World Health Assembly Recap: Financial Crunch, Affected Mandates, and Future Leadership
key_claim: US withdrawal and Western aid cuts forced WHO to cut its 2026-27 budget by 21% to $4.2bn, run a near-$1bn shortfall, shrink from 11 to 6 divisions, and drop its workforce nearly 10% to 8,569 in 2025.
frame_summary: US and Western funding withdrawal is forcing the WHO to shrink its budget, staff and mandate.
verbatim_quote: WHO's 2026–27 budget was slashed by 21%, to $4.2 billion from what was originally slated.
verbatim_list: WHO's budgetary cycle runs for two years; in the current biennium (2026–27) the organization is dealing with nearly a billion dollars of shortfall.

The financial crunch and restructuring led to a near 10% drop in WHO's total workforce, to 8,569 in 2025, according to a report on human resources delivered by Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus at the World Health Assembly.

title: 2026 AMR Benchmark: Pockets of progress from some companies show the tide can be turned, but there is no time to lose
date_evidence: The 2026 Antimicrobial Resistance Benchmark was published on 10 March 2026 by the Access to Medicine Foundation.
key_claim: The Access to Medicine Foundation's 2026 AMR Benchmark finds a 35% decline in large-company antibiotic pipelines over five years but identifies seven innovative late-stage projects that could counter resistance.
frame_summary: Big pharma keeps retreating from antibiotics, so sustaining the pipeline now depends on targeted incentives and a few surviving innovative projects.
verbatim_quote: While the Benchmark does find a 35% decline in the antimicrobial pipelines of LRBs, it also identifies seven late-stage projects that exhibit genuine innovation with potential to overcome resistance.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: New Global Consortium Aims to Transform Antibiotic Discovery to Counter the Growing AMR Crisis
key_claim: The Gates Foundation, Novo Nordisk Foundation and Wellcome awarded $60 million over three years to a new Gram-Negative Antibiotic Discovery Innovator consortium of 18 projects across 17 countries.
frame_summary: Philanthropic funders are using pooled grants as de facto industrial policy to rebuild the antibiotic pipeline that industry has abandoned.
